## Section 13.2: Introduction to `stringr`

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
med_djok_df <- read_csv(here("data/med_djok.csv"))
med_djok_df
```

```{r}
med_djok_df |> filter(str_detect(point, pattern = "@") == TRUE)
## keep only rows where the point ends with the @ symbol
## (so only rows that have points that end in an unforced error)
```

```{r}
med_djok_df |> filter(str_detect(point, pattern = "@") == TRUE) |>
  ## keep only rows where point has an @ in it
  mutate(error_type = case_when(str_detect(point, pattern = "d@") ~ "deep error",
                                str_detect(point, pattern = "w@") ~ "wide error",
                                str_detect(point, pattern = "n@") ~ "net error")) |>
  ## call a point that is d@ a "deep error", call a point that is w@ a 
 ## "wide error", and call a point that is n@ a "net error"
  group_by(PtWinner, error_type) |>
  summarise(n_errors = n())
  ## for each point winner and error type, give me the count
```

Exercise 4.

^something means "starts with the word something"

```{r}
med_djok_df |>
  mutate(serve_location = case_when(str_detect(point, "^4") ~ "wide",
                                    str_detect(point, "^5") ~ "body",
                                    str_detect(point, "^6") ~ "down the center")) |>
  relocate(serve_location)
```

Class Exercise 1.

```{r}
library(schrute)
schrute::theoffice

library(tidytext)
kevin_unnested <- theoffice |>
  filter(character == "Kevin") |>
  unnest_tokens("words", input = "text") |>
  relocate(words)

stop_words

extra_stop <- tibble(word = c("yeah", "hey", "gonna"))

kevin_nostop <- anti_join(kevin_unnested, stop_words, join_by(words == word)) |>
  anti_join(extra_stop, join_by(words == word))


kevin_top25 <- kevin_nostop |> group_by(words) |>
  summarise(n_say = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(n_say)) |>
  slice(1:25) |>
  mutate(words = fct_reorder(words, n_say))

ggplot(data = kevin_top25, aes(x = n_say, y = words)) +
  geom_col(colour = "skyblue4", fill = "skyblue1") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
kevin_unnested <- theoffice |>
  filter(character == "Kevin") |>
  unnest_tokens("words", input = "text") |>
  relocate(words)

kevin_speak <- kevin_unnested |> group_by(season) |>
  summarise(n_word_spoken = n())
## shows the total number of words for each season,
## but, each season has a different number of episodes

## what we could calculate instead is the average number of words per
## episode in each season.

## figure how many episodes there were in each season.
episode_df <- theoffice |> group_by(season) |>
  summarise(max_episode_number = max(episode))
## join the data set with episodes per season with the data set we just created
kevin_average <- inner_join(kevin_speak, episode_df, 
                            join_by(season == season)) |>
  mutate(words_per_episode = n_word_spoken / max_episode_number)

## figure out the average per episode and make a line plot.
ggplot(data = kevin_average, aes(x = season, y = words_per_episode)) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal() +
  lims(y = c(0, NA))
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = med_djok_df, aes(x = serve_location)) +
```

Your Turn 2.

```{r}
med_djok_df <- med_djok_df |> relocate(isSvrWinner) |>
  mutate(isSvrWinner = factor(isSvrWinner))

ggplot(data = med_djok_df, aes(x = serve_location)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = isSvrWinner, group = isSvrWinner)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Serving) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Your Turn 3.

```{r}
med_djok_df |> 
  mutate(is_volley = if_else(str_detect(point, "v") | str_detect(point, "z") |
                               str_detect(point, "i") | str_detect(point, "k"),
                             true = 1,
                             false = 0)) |>
  relocate(is_volley) |>
  summarise(prop_volley = mean(is_volley))
## 0.137 of all points in the match had a volley                             
```
